question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\left(2 x - 4\right) e^{- y - 3}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\left(2 x - 4\right) e^{- y - 3} \\ (e^{y + 3})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2 x - 4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (e^{y + 3})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (2 x - 4)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 3})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (2 x - 4)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 3})\,\text{d}y & =\int (2 x - 4)\,\text{d}x \\ e^{y + 3} & =\left(x - 2\right)^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
e^{y + 3}=\left(x - 2\right)^{2}+C.
$$

generation.domain: all real x,y; right side plus C>0

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{1 - \left(y + 3\right)^{2}}$ for $\,|\left(y+3\right)|<1.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sqrt{1 - \left(y + 3\right)^{2}} \\ (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y + 3\right)^{2}}})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y + 3\right)^{2}}})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y + 3\right)^{2}}})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (1)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \left(y + 3\right)^{2}}})\,\text{d}y & =\int (1)\,\text{d}x \\ \arcsin{\left(y + 3 \right)} & =x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\arcsin{\left(y + 3 \right)}=x+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=e^{x - 2} \cos^{2}{\left(y + 3 \right)}$ for $0<\left(y+3\right)<\frac{\pi }{2}.$

To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =e^{x - 2} \cos^{2}{\left(y + 3 \right)} \\ (\sec^{2}{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =e^{x - 2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\sec^{2}{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (e^{x - 2})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\sec^{2}{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (e^{x - 2})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\sec^{2}{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\text{d}y & =\int (e^{x - 2})\,\text{d}x \\ \tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} & =e^{x - 2}+C\end{aligned}

$$
\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)}=e^{x - 2}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{2}}{\left(y + 3\right)^{2}}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{2}}{\left(y + 3\right)^{2}} \\ (\left(y + 3\right)^{2})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\left(x - 2\right)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\left(y + 3\right)^{2})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\left(x - 2\right)^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\left(y + 3\right)^{2})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (\left(x - 2\right)^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\left(y + 3\right)^{2})\,\text{d}y & =\int (\left(x - 2\right)^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{\left(y + 3\right)^{3}}{3} & =\frac{\left(x - 2\right)^{3}}{3}+K \\ \left(y + 3\right)^{3} & =\left(x - 2\right)^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=3K.$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\left(y + 3\right)^{3}=\left(x - 2\right)^{3}+C.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\cos{\left(y + 3 \right)}}{\left(x - 2\right) \tan{\left(y + 3 \right)}} \\ (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x - 2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x - 2})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (\frac{1}{x - 2})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\text{d}y & =\int (\frac{1}{x - 2})\,\text{d}x \\ \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)} & =\ln{\left(\left|{x - 2}\right| \right)}+C\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\int (e^{y + 4})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (12 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 4})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (12 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ \int (e^{y + 4})\,\text{d}y & =\int (12 - 4 x)\,\text{d}x \\ e^{y + 4} & =- 2 \left(x - 3\right)^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
e^{y + 4}=- 2 \left(x - 3\right)^{2}+C.
$$
